metadata.scenario_context: James, Amy, and Lucas, who are colleagues at a technology startup, have recently been given the task to organize a company event to celebrate their startup's success in releasing their first app. The team has been buzzing about a recently published article claiming that the government is planning to lower corporate taxes which will greatly benefit their startup. They decide to discuss the details of the event

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Nicaragua have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest a vegetarian-friendly place for the celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss where to host the celebratory event.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message: I think we should celebrate our startup's success at Green Bites, it's a great vegetarian-friendly place. What do you think, James?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: James
shared_prefix.message: I think Green Bites is a good choice, but have you seen that article about the government planning to lower corporate taxes? I'm not sure I believe it, I mean, can we really trust what the press says?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message: I've seen the article and I think it's credible. We have a free press in this country and I believe they do a good job of reporting the facts. I'm confident that if they're saying the government is planning to lower corporate taxes, it's likely true.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: James
shared_prefix.message: I'm not so sure... I've seen many times where the press gets it wrong or has an agenda. Back home in Nicaragua, we've learned to take what the press says with a grain of salt. I'd like to discuss this more, but first, about the event, do you think Green Bites can accommodate all of our colleagues?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message: Yes, Green Bites has a large event space, I've checked. They can definitely accommodate our team. And regarding the press, I understand your skepticism, but I still have faith in the American press to report accurately.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: James
shared_prefix.message: That's good to know about Green Bites. As for the press, I just don't share your faith... I think we should be careful about what we believe. Have you considered other venues, just in case Green Bites doesn't work out?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message: I think we're getting a bit sidetracked with the press discussion, but I do want to address it. Deep down, we are all the same, and people are pretty much motivated by the same things - we want accurate information, right? When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us, seeking truth and transparency. I believe the press is a fundamental part of that, and some values are just universal, like the importance of a free press in a democratic society. Let's focus on the event, but I do think our faith in the press is something we can both get behind, we both know, at the end of the day, that it's essential for our country's success.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: James
turns.message: I understand what you're saying, but I still have my doubts about the press. Let's focus on the event, like you said. So, what's the plan for food and drinks at Green Bites? Should we go with their standard catering options or try to customize the menu?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Lucas
turns.message: I'm glad we're moving forward with the event planning. Green Bites has a great selection of vegetarian options, and I think we should customize the menu to fit our team's tastes. They have a variety of vegan and gluten-free options as well, so we can make sure everyone has something they like. By the way, don't you think the press would have reported if Green Bites had any major issues with their food or service?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: James
turns.message: I wouldn't count on the press to always report the truth... but yeah, customizing the menu is a good idea. Let's make sure to include some traditional Nicaraguan dishes, that would be a nice touch. And as for the press reporting on Green Bites, I'm sure they'd only report what suits their agenda.
turns.label: Defense

positive.mediator_utterance: I'm hearing that you both have different perspectives shaped by your unique experiences with media and press - Lucas, from an American context of institutional trust, and James, from a Nicaraguan background of media skepticism. Could you each share a bit about how your specific cultural contexts have influenced your views on media credibility? I'm curious to understand the nuanced stories behind your different starting points.
